mode: built-in image_gen, reference-guided style transfer and refinement
initial_prompt: Use case: style-transfer. Create ONE landscape concept image that LOOKS LIKE A LOW-POLY 3D GAME RENDER for Duck Rails, using the attached images as explicit references. Image 1 is the existing train concept: preserve its long mostly OPEN-AIR roofless crew deck, compact lightly enclosed front driving shelter, teal/ivory paint, warm amber lights, overall low utility-train silhouette, coal furnace, simple rails, backpack hooks, shared gear and space for eight low-moving players. Images 2 and 3 are actual DuckZ avatars and textured props: authoritative style reference for low polygon geometry, strong facets, oversized white eyeballs with tiny black pupils, orange/yellow beaks, rounded torso ending without legs, long gorilla-like arms with hands. Image 4 is the actual DuckZ environment: authoritative reference for simple box-built industrial assets and visibly coarse pixelated textures. Image 5 is DuckZ key art: reference for vivid yellow duck color, orange beak, broad low-poly facets and chunky square texture pixels; do NOT copy its combat scene. Transform the first image's watercolor train into a convincing economical low-poly realtime-game-style asset render, with crisp flat polygon faces and low-resolution visibly pixelated color textures (Minecraft-like pixel texels on conventional low-poly meshes, NOT Minecraft voxel cubes). Make the pixel texture pattern clearly visible on teal paint, off-white trim, wood deck, coal and bags. Use simple flat boxes and low-sided cylinders, low-sided wheels, straight rail segments, bevels only where silhouette benefits. Eliminate fine rivets, dense pipes, ornate lantern cages, detailed suspension, tiny cracks, realistic corrosion and painterly marks; express wear using sparse coarse texture pixels. The TRAIN is the hero: large three-quarter front-side view fills most of the canvas, long open deck receding to the right; show unobstructed deck space, multiple wide side boarding gaps. Crucial functional constraint: player eye height only about 0.5m ABOVE THE DECK. Window glass/opening must extend down near the floor, with a thin sill well below that eye line, very low short nose and controls to the side, no tall opaque panel/dashboard in front of the driver. Keep rail panels very low so low avatars can see over; only front has small roof. Furnace mouth reachable from crew side, warm inside. Include just THREE accurate DuckZ-style avatars for scale, with NO LEGS OR FEET, short low hovering torsos, long arms/hands, enormous eyes and angular duck bills; one driving low at the front, one beside a backpack, one at rear. Use existing avatar design language from refs, NOT the white real-bird silhouettes in image 1, not human bodies or tiny wings. Avoid copying any weapons/coins from the refs. A small clearly separated inset at bottom right shows first-person forward sightline from 0.5m above deck, with the window almost to floor and rails visible beyond; label only '0.5 m eye height'. Background a minimal dark desaturated railway yard with angular evergreen silhouettes and a simple warehouse to echo Quackville; it should stay subdued and not compete. Render look: clear conventional game lighting, modest ambient shading, simple shadows, warm furnace and lights against cold night, main train geometry and pixel textures readable. Sharp image with pixelated MATERIAL TEXTURES, NOT entire-image pixelation. No paper, no sketches, no ink contours, no watercolor, no smooth high-poly toy/Pixar appearance, no photorealistic PBR gloss, no dense microgeometry, no raytraced spectacle. This is an exploratory AI concept image, not a claim of an actual Unity asset or performance proof. Small unobtrusive title 'DUCK RAILS / LOW-POLY TRAIN'.
refinement_prompt: Refine the attached train image, keeping its teal and ivory industrial train design, main three-quarter camera, long roofless open crew deck, front-only shelter, location, warm lamps, title and lower-right inset. Use images 2 and 3 as the authoritative DuckZ material/geometry reference. Make these precise changes: (1) the pixelation is painted FLAT on broad simple low-poly polygon surfaces, not built from hundreds of tiny voxel bricks. Remove the little raised cubes, chunky bevels, individually modeled planks, tread blocks and rivets. Body side is a single flat plane with a visibly low-resolution texture. Wheels are simple 8-sided dark discs with basic axles. Rails are simple straight low-sided bars. Floor a flat plane with a coarse wood-plank texture. Hardware reduced to a handful of broad shapes. Match actual low-poly game asset complexity in images 2/3, preserving sharp chunky texel squares. (2) CRUCIAL lower the entire front windshield bottom edge to just above deck, so a player's eyes only 0.5 metres above DECK see the railway clearly. Move the furnace to an inward-facing low side unit behind the front shelter, not under the windshield. Front face below window is a very shallow solid panel, not a tall furnace wall. Remove driver's seat and any stool/perch. Driver is a legless DuckZ torso low over deck with long arms, eyes level with LOWER portion of windshield. Remove the stool beneath the gorilla character too; all avatars are legless torsos with long arms and no feet, per reference 2. In the inset, show a VERY low sill almost touching deck and controls off to right; no obstructing dashboard. Keep the small '0.5 m eye height' label. (3) Retain real-time 3D game render appearance, but reduce glossy highlights, cinematic detail and toy-like rounded geometry. Broad low-poly flat faces, low-resolution pixel textures, straightforward game lighting. The ground should be a flat gravel plane with a pixel texture, not many extruded cubes. Do not alter the open crew layout or add any roof over it. Final image is a visual concept, not an implemented model.
